messages.author: 59cc3d5f9c3a71af
messages.subject: Statistical dilemma regarding multigroup analysis
parts:
I analyzing quite simple data with multigroup analysis .

 However, I facing a statistical dilemma that limits my

 understanding of the data.


 In short, my data includes one dependent variable, one mediator, and

 few independent variables. The dependent and mediator variables have a

 distinct non-normal distribution that is skewed to the left. The

 multivariate test of Normality support non-multivariate normal

 distribution although the fit to a normal distribution is better than

 to a Gamma distribution.


 I read that the MLR estimator is robust to models with

 non-multivariate normal distribution, so I run the SEM models on

 the original variables with MLR as an estimator. However, in parallel

 we have also tried to transform the whole model with a Box-Cox

 transformation, which indeed made the multivariate distribution

 normal. However, when we run the SEM model on the transformed data,

 using the ML estimation we get completely different qualitative

 results (e.g., different models are chosen based on AICc). I was

 wondering what is more correct, to run the SEM model on the original

 data with MLR and non-multivariate normal distribution or transform the data and use ML.


 Many thanks, Ron

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Statistical dilemma regarding multigroup analysis
parts:
Ron

It doesnt surprise me that the results differ when you transform the data. This because when you transform it, the data is basically in a different scale, now the interpretation has to be in function of the transformation instead of the actual scale of the data.

For example, if you log transform a variable/predictor, now the beta is represents the change in the outcome for 1 logunits. This is the main reason I dont like to transform data, the scale becomes hard to interpret. 

I would recommend to keep the data in its original scale and adjust the test. This way the interpretation of the parameters are in a interpretable metric

bye
